claims.claim: grid-scale horizontal diffusivity K = 3.6 × 10⁻⁴ L^1.07 m² s⁻¹ (code: 3.6e-4 × 50^1.07 ≈ 0.024 m²/s at the 50-m cell)
claims.source_value: 3.6 × 10⁻⁴ ℓ^1.07 is the fit to the Twin West Lake central releases alone (N = 37); the authors' line for all three data sets (N = 105) is K = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ ℓ^1.10 (eq. 8)
claims.location: p. 1524 (PDF p. 6), Table 2; eq. 8 on p. 1525 (PDF p. 7)
claims.conditions: apparent diffusivity of dye patches against patch size ℓ = 3σ_rc (m), α in m^(2−β) s⁻¹; central dye releases in the epilimnion (~3 m) of Twin West Lake, a small sheltered oligotrophic lake in British Columbia, 2, 18 and 24 August 1988, wind ~1 m/s; Twin West patch sizes ~10–50 m (Table 1)
claims.note: the digits are the Twin West-only regression, not the paper's headline relation; at ℓ = 50 m the two give the same K (≈0.024 m²/s), and the authors put the 95 % band at a factor of ~2.5 either side. A grid cell is not a dye patch: using ℓ = cell size is the project's choice

notes: Table 2 rows (read from the raw text order; the -layout extraction misaligns them): Okubo N 57, 2.8e-4, β 1.10; Murthy N 11, 6.6e-5, 1.35; Twin West central N 37, 3.6e-4, 1.07; Okubo+Murthy N 68, 2.5e-4, 1.13; all three N 105, 3.2e-4, 1.10 (r 0.99), which the abstract calls valid from 10 m to more than 100 km. If the rewrite wants the authors' recommended relation, cite eq. 8 (3.2 × 10⁻⁴ ℓ^1.1); the model's value does not change at 50 m. Shore releases dispersed faster than central ones (Table 1, K up to ~0.02 m²/s).
